human_economic_burden.boundary: Dependence on melt from glaciers and snow; not glacier-only water-supply share and not a count experiencing shortage.

persistence.small_glacier_region_peak_water_status: most have likely passed peak water

source_locators: WMO State of Global Water Resources 2024, Snow cover and glaciers chapter: 450 Gt lost, all 19 regions, third consecutive year.
WMO report methods: approximately 500 field glaciers and more than 200,000 geodetically measured glaciers, covering 96 percent of global glaciers.
UN International Year of Glaciers Preservation key message 7: more than 2 billion people rely on melt from glaciers and snow for freshwater.
excluded_from_scoring: coastal population exposed to sea-level rise
mountain-water users not explicitly tied to glacier or snow melt

transformations.formula: Normalize the source-reported 2024 global glacier mass loss through a fixed gigatonne range; retain sea-level equivalent as context only.
Normalize the official lower-bound population relying on glacier-and-snow melt while preserving its snow-inclusive exposure boundary.
Use the source-reported third consecutive all-region loss year and divide 19 loss regions by 19 assessed regions.

receipts.uncertainty: The WMO global mass estimate combines about 500 field-monitored glaciers and geodetic measurements covering more than 200,000 glaciers. Preliminary 2024 observations, regional scaling and mass-balance methods affect the estimate. The human figure covers melt from glaciers and snow and must not be interpreted as glacier-only volume share or observed shortage.
receipts.freshness: WMO State of Global Water Resources 2024 and UN glacier-water assessment 2025; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T18:12:40.094Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: Official global assessments quantify glacier mass loss, glacier-and-snow meltwater dependence, consecutive persistence and complete glacier-region extent.
higher_priority_failures: No harmonized current global series measures glacier-derived runoff as a share of seasonal human water supply, so the current-data method does not pass the exact node contract.
